To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the prognosis of pancreatic adenocarcinoma patients with high fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) uptake is significantly worse compared to patients with lower FDG uptake.

the use of FDG-PET for pancreatic cancer staging has not been shown to improve overall survival, but may be useful for identifying patients with a poor prognosis who may benefit from aggressive therapy.
the prognosis of pancreatic cancer patients with high FDG uptake in PET/CT is significantly worse than that of patients without high FDG uptake.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of a new technique of positron emission tomog- raphy (PET) using fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG), which is a glucose analog with a positron emitting nuclide (F-18) attached.
the study of the relationship between the use of fluorodeoxyglucose (18F) positron emission tomographic (PET) scanning and the prognosis of patients with pancreatic carcinoma.
the development and application of a new class of fluorine-containing compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FDG PET has no role in the diagnosis of pancreatic cancer.
FDG-PET is not a useful tool for diagnosing pancreatic carcinoma, but it may be used for the staging of pancreatic carcinoma.
the use of FDG-PET in the management of pancreatic cancer is still investigational.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of 18F-FDG PET/CT in the diagnosis of pancreatic carcinoma is not as accurate as previously thought.
we have demonstrated that the use of 18F-FDG-PET/CT is useful for staging pancreatic cancer and for monitoring treatment response.
we are able to identify the most relevant prognostic factors in patients with pancreatic cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of metastatic disease is a significant risk factor for poor prognosis.
the presence of metastatic disease in the liver and/or lungs at the time of diagnosis is a negative prognostic factor in pancreatic cancer.
